newsitem.title: USA: New jury sworn in for O.J. Simpson civil trial.
newsitem.headline: New jury sworn in for O.J. Simpson civil trial.

text.p: A new jury, the second in two days, was sworn in for the O.J. Simpson civil trial on Friday.
The reconstituted jury is made up of seven women and five men. The racial makeup is eight whites, one black, one Hispanic, one of mixed white and Hispanic heritage, and one part Asian, part black.

A black juror in his 40's, later identified as Edgar Allen, was excused earlier Friday from the original jury by Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki for alcohol misconduct after fellow jurors had complained that they smelled alcohol on his breath.
Lawyers for both sides were then allowed to use peremptory challenges on the remaining panelists resulting in two of the 11 being excused and replaced, in addition to the replacement for Allen.

Simpson, who was acquitted by a predominantly black jury at a criminal trial last year of murdering his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, has been sued in civil court by the families of the victims.
If found responsible for the murders, the former football star could be forced to pay millions of dollars in damages.
